get.description: Open a WebSocket here and send an `auth` message within 10 seconds, and again whenever the token is renewed. The server answers `ready` and a `snapshot` of the transfers in progress. Administrators can `subscribe` to other users; every subscribe is answered with a new snapshot, and your own events always arrive. Messages are described by the ClientMessage and EventMessage schemas. The connection closes with code 4401 when authentication fails or the token expires without renewal.

get.description:
Free text matches names fuzzily: substrings, abbreviations such as `invq3` for invoice_q3.pdf, and small typos. It also matches the text inside files when the server reads it, including text recognised in images and scans; every word must appear, and quotes match a phrase. Name matches come first. Tags narrow the results; they have the form `key<op>values`:

- `type` (also `kind`, `is`): `folder`, `file`, a top-level MIME type (`image`, `video`, `text`…), an extension, a MIME subtype or a whole MIME type, such as `type=image,pdf,md` or `type=application/zip`
- `ext`: extensions only
- `in`: a folder and everything below it, such as `in="/My Docs"`
- `modified` (also `date`): `2024`, `2024-06`, `2024-06-15`, `today`, `yesterday`, or a relative `7d`, `2w`, `3m`, `1y`
- `size`: such as `10mb`, `500kb`, `1.5gb`

Operators are `=` or `:` (is), `!=` or a leading `-` (is not), and `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=` for modified and size. Commas separate alternatives, separate tags must all hold, and `modified=a..b` or `size=a..b` is a range. A relative date is a moment: `modified>7d` is newer than a week ago.
